title: Looking for a Newcastle leasing agent? You might need a tenant representative instead
excerpt: A landlord's leasing agent and a tenant representative sit on different sides of the same transaction. Here is how the roles differ.
author: Joe Kelley
metaDescription: Understand the difference between a landlord's leasing agent and tenant-side commercial lease representation in Newcastle and the Hunter.
body:
A commercial lease negotiation has two sides. The agent appointed to lease the property acts for the landlord. A tenant representative is engaged to advise the business that will occupy the space.

That distinction matters because the parties may have different priorities around rent, incentives, lease flexibility, make-good obligations and delivery timing.

## What a landlord's leasing agent does

The landlord's agent markets the premises, manages enquiries and negotiates the transaction for the property owner. They can provide useful information about the building and proposed terms, but their client is the landlord.

## What a tenant representative does

A tenant representative works from the occupying business's brief. The role can include:

- clarifying location, space, timing and operational requirements
- identifying and assessing suitable leasing options
- comparing rent, outgoings, incentives and other commercial terms
- negotiating the commercial position with the landlord's agent
- coordinating with the tenant's solicitor and project team
- keeping decisions, risks and next actions visible through signing and handover

Legal advice remains the role of the tenant's solicitor. Tenant representation provides the commercial context and negotiation support around that legal review.

## Why the full occupancy cost matters

Headline rent is only one part of a lease decision. Outgoings, incentives, review mechanisms, fit out requirements, make-good obligations, options and timing can materially change the overall position.

A useful comparison puts those elements side by side and records the assumptions, evidence and trade-offs behind the recommendation.

## How fees work

Fee arrangements depend on the engagement and transaction structure. Scope, fees and any relevant payment arrangements should be explained before work begins.
